label: thorough-high-webfetch
prompt:
You are reviewing pull request #${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} as a code reviewer.
The PR's head is checked out in the working directory. Its diff against the base
branch is in ${{ runner.temp }}/pr.diff; read it first. Then read every file the diff
touches in full, and the unchanged code it calls or is called by: a bug often lies in
how the change interacts with code it doesn't touch. Follow the repository's own
conventions (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/ and .github/instructions/ where present).

Your review may be the only one this PR gets before it merges on its own, so be
thorough. For each change, ask what happens on the paths the author didn't test:
another event or trigger, a rerun, a skipped or cancelled job, a different actor
(a bot, an app, a person without write access), an empty or malformed input, a
race between two runs. For GitHub Actions workflows and merge gates, reason about
how GitHub itself behaves: which events fire, what a skipped or failed check does
to a PR's mergeStateStatus, who the actor is, what each token can do. Look hardest
at code that decides whether something merges, releases or gets permissions.

Report every real problem a maintainer would want fixed or knowingly accepted
before merging: bugs, security issues, broken edge cases, missing or wrong tests,
and clear departures from the repository's conventions. Don't report style nits or
praise. Every finding names a file path relative to the repository root and a line
number on the new side, preferably a line the diff adds or shows as context, and
says what goes wrong, in which situation, and how to fix it.

Answer with a short summary of the change and your verdict, and your findings.

review.summary:
PR #298 adds a "Claude Review" backup to Copilot's review. The new workflow `claude-review.yml` has a review job and a post job. The review job runs claude-code-action with read-only tools on same-repo PRs carrying the `review:claude` label. The post job runs `post_claude_review.py`, which posts the findings as one COMMENT review from github-actions[bot], pinned to the head commit and starting with `<!-- claude-review -->`. `pr-automerge.yml` now accepts a marker review of the head in place of Copilot's. It counts Claude's and Copilot's rounds together toward the review cap, and it lets Claude's unresolved threads be bypassed at the cap. Two unrelated changes ride along: `release_post.py` now normalises the spacing after quote and list markers in commit subjects, and `ci.yml` drops the `ready_for_review` trigger and adds a 10-minute timeout on the Playwright install.

I read the diff and the surrounding code. I did not run any of the tests or workflows, so GitHub-behaviour points below are reasoned, not observed. The auto-merge JS looks correct, and its tests match its logic. The `release_post.py` change looks fine. My concerns are the merge-gate trust boundary, the stale-head and duplicate-review behaviour of the post script, and how fragile the "hold the merge" mechanism is. Verdict: not ready to merge as is. The first finding should be fixed or knowingly accepted. The rest are smaller.

findings.body: The post job runs on `pull_request`, so both the workflow file and the `post_claude_review.py` it checks out come from the PR's own merge ref. Auto-merge now treats any github-actions[bot] review that starts with `<!-- claude-review -->` as a satisfied review of the head. A PR can therefore edit `claude-review.yml` or `post_claude_review.py` to post a "No findings" marked review on its own head, and the job has `pull-requests: write` to do it. `pr-automerge.yml` is deliberately a `pull_request_target`/main-only file so a PR can't edit the thing that decides whether it merges (see its header comment); this reopens that hole. It matters most for agent-authored PRs (Sandcastle). The marker is also forgeable by any other workflow that posts as github-actions[bot]. Fix options: take the post script from the base branch (check out `github.base_ref`, or move posting into a `workflow_run`/`pull_request_target` workflow that runs main's copy). Or at minimum document that Claude Review is a soft gate that a PR author can bypass.

Claude runs with `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` in its environment while reading attacker-influenced content: the PR diff and head checkout. For Sandcastle PRs that includes text derived from issues. Its output is then posted verbatim as public review comments. `--allowedTools Read` does not stop prompt-injected text from making Claude `Read` `/proc/self/environ` or `~/.claude/*` and echo the token into a finding. The checked-out head's `.claude/settings.json` hooks and `.mcp.json` are also loaded by Claude Code in that same working directory, and they can execute commands with the token. Fix: add deny rules for those paths (for example `Read(/proc/**)`, `Read(~/.claude/**)`). Run Claude from a directory without the PR's project settings (check the PR out into a subdirectory and `--add-dir` it, or delete `.claude/` and `.mcp.json` from the checkout). Consider also treating the posted text as untrusted.

The commentable lines come from `pull_files(args.pr)`, which is the PR's current files, but the review is pinned to `commit_id=args.head`. If a push lands after Claude reviewed the old head (the old review is not cancelled once its review job has finished, and a rerun of an old run has the same problem), the line numbers are checked against the new diff and sent against the old commit. GitHub then either rejects the whole review with a 422 or anchors comments on the wrong lines. Fix: read the PR's current head SHA first, and skip posting (exit 0) if it is not `--head`. Or compute the diff lines from the compare of base...head instead of the live `/pulls/N/files`.

Posting is not idempotent. Re-adding the `review:claude` label, re-running the workflow or re-running the failed post job creates another full review on the same head. That duplicates every inline thread, and each copy is a new unresolved thread that blocks auto-merge until it is resolved. A rerun after an off-diff failure also re-posts the same inline comments. Fix: before posting, list the PR's reviews and skip, or only update, when a marked review already exists for `--head`.

Both `subprocess.run(..., check=True, capture_output=True)` calls hide `gh`'s stderr. A failure (422 for a bad line or commit, 403, 404) surfaces as a bare `CalledProcessError` traceback with the command and exit code, but not the API error message. The step then fails with nothing the maintainer can act on. Catch `CalledProcessError`, print `error.stderr`, and exit 1.

The "hold the merge" guarantee for off-diff findings rests entirely on this step exiting 1 so that a non-required check fails and the PR goes UNSTABLE. That has gaps. (a) The review is created before the job fails, so a PR Auto-Merge evaluation in that window (the schedule sweep, or another workflow_run) sees a marker review of the head, no threads, and possibly a not-yet-failed check, and may merge. (b) Off-diff findings are likely to be common, since the model is only prompted, not constrained, to use diff lines. Each one leaves the PR stuck until someone pushes. (c) Rerunning the job does not clear it, because it just fails again. A more robust design: snap an off-diff finding to the nearest diff line in the same file, or post it as an unresolved thread (or a file-level comment). Failing that, post the review as one that blocks, so auto-merge sees a real unresolved thread.

Test coverage is thin for the logic that decides whether the whole review is accepted. `diff_lines` has no test for the `\ No newline at end of file` marker. It also has no test for renamed files, multi-file input, or a trailing empty row after `split("\n")` (which would register a phantom line). `GitHub.pull_files` (`--paginate --slurp`, multiple pages) and `create_review` are never exercised, and there is no test for a non-positive `line` or an oversized `FINDINGS`. The `claude-review.yml` job `if` (bot actor, label, draft, dependabot) is untested, and the only workflow test in `pr-automerge.test.mjs` is a regex on the trigger list. Add cases for those, especially the `\` row and pagination.

review.summary:
PR #298 adds a label-triggered "Claude Review" workflow, `claude-review.yml`. It is a backup for Copilot reviews. A read-only job runs Claude on the PR diff and emits JSON. A second job (`post_claude_review.py`) posts that JSON as one `github-actions[bot]` COMMENT review marked with `<!-- claude-review -->`. Findings that can't be inline comments go in the review body under a second off-diff marker. `pr-automerge.yml` now accepts a marked Claude review as the reviewer of the head. Claude and Copilot rounds share the 3-round cap, and an off-diff marker holds the merge. The PR also bundles two unrelated changes: a `release_post.py` whitespace-collapsing tweak, and a CI edit that drops the `ready_for_review` trigger and adds a Playwright install timeout. I couldn't run the Python or Node tests (no shell in this session), so this is a read-through only.

Verdict: request changes. The main problem is that the off-diff path fails the post check. That leaves the PR UNSTABLE, so the "merge past off-diff findings at the cap" branch (and the test for it) can't happen in production. The marker that the merge gate trusts can also be forged from a PR branch. The rest are smaller.

findings.body: The off-diff path exits 1, so the `Post Claude's review` check fails on the head commit. The failing check is not a required check, so GitHub reports the PR as UNSTABLE. `pr-automerge.yml` only merges when `mergeStateStatus === "CLEAN"` (line 321), and the claude-review.yml header comment says the same about a failed run here. So the "merges past off-diff findings at the review cap" branch (pr-automerge.yml:309/332) and its test never happen in production. The test fakes a CLEAN PR. A PR at the cap with an off-diff finding sits UNSTABLE until a new push. The next push gets another Claude review, which can fail the same way. That is the review-chasing loop the cap exists to stop. The failing exit is also redundant, because the `OFF_DIFF_MARKER` already holds the merge. Fix: don't exit non-zero (use a warning annotation), or have the cap path not depend on that check's conclusion. Also add a test that covers the check state.

The merge gate trusts any `github-actions[bot]` review whose body starts with `CLAUDE_MARKER`, and nothing authenticates that review. `claude-review.yml` runs on `pull_request`, so for a same-repo PR the PR's own copy of the workflow and of `post_claude_review.py` run with `pull-requests: write`. The branch author can edit either one, or add a workflow, to post a marked, finding-free review of the head. That satisfies the "a reviewer reviewed the head" gate. Posting three such reviews on three distinct commits reaches the cap, which then ignores the unresolved Copilot threads. This is the situation the header of pr-automerge.yml avoids by using `pull_request_target`: "a PR can't edit the script that decides whether it merges". Fix: keep the poster out of the PR's control, for example run the post step from `pull_request_target`/`workflow_run` using main's copy. Otherwise record in the PR description that this widens the gate to anyone with push access.

`Read,Glob,Grep` are unrestricted, and the PR diff is untrusted prompt input. A prompt-injected diff could make Claude read `/proc/self/environ`, `~/.claude`, or anything under the `--add-dir ${{ runner.temp }}` directory. That includes `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` in the action's environment. Claude could then put the contents in a finding body, which the post job publishes as a PR comment. This only applies to same-repo PRs, because fork PRs get no secrets. Still, the "Claude never holds a write token" guarantee doesn't cover exfiltrating the read secret. Consider `--add-dir` limited to just the diff file, deny rules for paths outside the workspace, and a note in the header about the same-repo-only assumption.

The `if` skips bot actors. It does not handle a human who lacks write access, such as a triager adding `review:claude`. As far as I can tell, `claude-code-action` checks that the actor has write permission and errors out otherwise. The `Review with Claude` check then fails and the PR goes UNSTABLE, which is exactly the outcome the comment above this `if` says it avoids for bots. Fix: gate on actor permission, or set `allowed_non_write_users`, or have the secret-check step also detect this case and succeed with a notice.

The post step isn't idempotent and doesn't check that `HEAD_SHA` is still the PR head. A re-run of the failed post job (the off-diff case always fails) creates a second review with the same inline comments, so every duplicated thread needs resolving. `pull_files` reads the PR's current files while the review is pinned to the older `commit_id`. After a push during the run, line numbers valid for the current diff can be wrong for the older commit. GitHub then rejects the whole review with a 422, or the finding is wrongly classified as off-diff. Fix: in the script, skip posting (exit 0) when the PR's current head differs from `--head`, and skip when a marked review of `--head` already exists.

PROCESS.md, which AGENTS.md makes the process source of truth, still says only Copilot's review and Copilot rounds gate the merge. This PR changes the gate. A Claude review (via the `review:claude` label) now counts, Claude and Copilot rounds share the cap of 3, and an off-diff marker holds the merge. Update the Review/Auto-Merge bullets, and add the new `review:claude` label and its bot-actor and secret caveats.

The `release_post.py` marker-whitespace change and its test edits, plus the `ci.yml` changes (dropping `ready_for_review`, Playwright `timeout-minutes`), have nothing to do with Claude Review. They are separate behaviour changes bundled into a merge-gate PR, which makes both harder to review and to revert. Split them into their own PRs. If the `ci.yml` and `release_post.py` changes stay, the PR description should justify them.

review.summary:
PR #298 adds a "Claude Review" backup reviewer for when Copilot's review budget is used up. It adds three things:

- A new `claude-review.yml` workflow runs `claude-code-action` read-only on PRs labelled `review:claude`.
- A new `post_claude_review.py` posts the findings as one COMMENT review from github-actions[bot]. Findings on diff lines become inline threads. Findings off the diff go in the body under an off-diff marker.
- `pr-automerge.yml` now accepts a marked Claude review of the head in place of Copilot's. It counts Claude reviews toward the review cap and ignores Claude's threads once the cap is reached. It holds the merge on the off-diff marker until the cap. `ci.yml` stops running on `ready_for_review` and gets a Playwright install timeout. A `release_post.py` commit-subject change is bundled in.

The auto-merge logic and the tests look consistent. Verdict: don't merge yet, because of one significant gap. The design relies on never failing a check, since a failed check leaves the PR UNSTABLE and PR Auto-Merge never merges it. But the likeliest failure of the new workflow, Claude being unavailable, does fail a check. I found no correctness bug in the `pr-automerge.yml` changes. `ci.yml`, the `release_post.py` change and the tests were fine apart from the findings below.

findings.body:
The workflow says a failed check must be avoided because it leaves the PR UNSTABLE and PR Auto-Merge never merges it, even at the cap. But most failure modes of the review job still fail the check:

- The `Review` step fails when the OAuth token has expired or is revoked, the quota or rate limit is hit, or the API is down. That is the situation this backup exists for.
- The action fails on an actor without write access.
- Claude returns no `structured_output`. `FINDINGS` is then empty, and `post_claude_review.py` exits 1 as malformed (line 154).
- The `gh api` POST fails.

Every one of these leaves a red `Review with Claude` or `Post Claude's review` check on the head. The PR then sits UNSTABLE until someone pushes or re-runs, and the review cap can't rescue it.

Fix: set `continue-on-error: true` on the `Review` step. Have the `post` job turn a missing or malformed result into a `::warning::` and a pass. Make the `gh api` failure path a warning too, or at least document that the backup can deadlock the PR.

`create_review` runs `gh api` with `capture_output=True, check=True` and discards the output. On failure the step shows only `CalledProcessError ... returned non-zero exit status 1`, and the API's error message is lost. GitHub rejects the whole review with a 422 if any inline comment can't be resolved. That can happen if the PR files list and the review API disagree about a line, or if the head moved. One such comment then fails the whole review.

Fix: print `error.stderr` and `error.stdout` on failure. On a 422, retry once with every finding moved into the body, which would also carry the off-diff marker. That way one bad line doesn't cost the review.

Skipping when `github.actor` ends in `[bot]` silently drops the review for the head. That covers a push by an agent or bot account, and a `review:claude` label added by a bot or by `GITHUB_TOKEN`. The PR then has no Claude review of that head and stays pending, with no signal on the PR. Copilot is out of budget in exactly this scenario, so nothing else will review it. The comment says the next person's push or a re-added label fixes it, but a PR driven only by agents has no such person.

Consider checking the PR author or the label's actor differently, or posting a PR comment or notice when the review is skipped for this reason. Otherwise, state this limitation in the PR Auto-Merge docs.

`--allowedTools "Read,Glob,Grep"` is a blanket Read grant with no path scope. In a headless run, Claude can read anything on the runner, including `/proc/self/environ` and files under `_temp`. Those hold `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, and `${{ github.token }}` is passed to the action as `github_token`. Everything Claude returns is published verbatim as a PR review comment. Diff text, commit messages and file contents are untrusted input, so a prompt injection in them could get the model to echo secrets into a public comment.

Fork PRs get no secrets, which limits the exposure, but any same-repo branch with copied-in untrusted content is still affected. Scope Read to the workspace and `RUNNER_TEMP/pr.diff` (path-scoped `Read(...)` rules). Alternatively, move the diff into the workspace and drop `--add-dir`. Consider also scanning the findings for token patterns before posting.
